definition: The total random kinetic energy of the particles of a system plus the total intermolecular potential energy from the forces between them; it is a total, unlike temperature, which measures the average kinetic energy per particle.
Energy transferred from a body at a higher temperature to one at a lower temperature because of their temperature difference, often called heat; it is energy in transit, not something a body stores.
The state of bodies in thermal contact that are at the same temperature, so there is no resultant thermal energy transfer between them.

A change of state, such as melting, freezing, boiling or condensing, that happens at constant temperature for a pure substance; the energy transferred changes the intermolecular potential energy of the particles, not their average random kinetic energy.
The energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K, in $\text{J kg}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}$, so that $Q = mc\Delta T$.
The energy needed to change the phase of 1 kg of a substance at constant temperature, in $\text{J kg}^{-1}$, so that $Q = mL$; fusion (melting) and vaporization (boiling) have different values.
